scenario: AITA For Selling My Former Roommates Games | So a few years ago I was renting this place with this dude and we were on a lease. When the lease was nearing it's end he just peaced out. We're talking took most of everything leaving only the last bit of his half of rent and a few things he said in a note he didn't want to bring with him. Thing with where I live is that if you don't discard of things on your own when you move out the landlord can pay to have someone remove the stuff. We're talking cases of dudes having $250 taken off their deposit just for some dude to take 3 milk crates of things to the dump. It's a rip off. I texted and emailed him for 2 weeks asking to pick these things up or take them to the dump but he never responded. So I took most of his things to the dump but he also had around 60 video games for PS4. So I figured I'd sell them. There is a local game store where they buy used games and they gave me $600 for all of his games. Well cut to last week and I was at a party he was at and we were polite. He then asks how the move out was and I said good, and naturally he asked what I did with his stuff. He got mad when he found out I sold his games but I told him that I tried to get him to grab these things but he never reached out. He's now calling me an asshole and asking me to pay him back. I checked and legally there's nothing there but now I'm wondering if I'm the asshole for doing this.

We're talking took most of everything leaving only the last bit of his half of rent and a few things he said in a note he didn't want to bring with him. Thing with where I live is that if you don't discard of things on your own when you move out the landlord can pay to have someone remove the stuff. We're talking cases of dudes having $250 taken off their deposit just for some dude to take 3 milk crates of things to the dump. It's a rip off. I texted and emailed him for 2 weeks asking to pick these things up or take them to the dump but he never responded. So I took most of his things to the dump but he also had around 60 video games for PS4. So I figured I'd sell them. There is a local game store where they buy used games and they gave me $600 for all of his games. Well cut to last week and I was at a party he was at and we were polite. He then asks how the move out was and I said good, and naturally he asked what I did with his stuff. He got mad when he found out I sold his games but I told him that I tried to get him to grab these things but he never reached out. He's now calling me an asshole and asking me to pay him back. I checked and legally there's nothing there but now I'm wondering if I'm the asshole for doing this.

Answer: <0 or 1>

prediction.raw: **1** (Not the asshole) **Why:** - **Abandonment is clear:** Your roommate physically left, only provided partial rent, and explicitly stated in a note that some items were " things he didn't want to bring." He then ignored *multiple* attempts to contact him over two weeks ( texts and emails). This is textbook abandonment—not a " I forgot to pick up my stuff" situation. - **You acted to protect yourself:** The landlord would have deduct $250 from *your* deposit if you didn dispose of the items (as you described). By clearing the non-game items and selling the games, you prevented a financial loss *to yourself*. - **No legal obligation:** You confirmed " legally there's nothing there"—meaning no laws require you to return the $600 or hold the items. In virtually all U.S. states, abandoned property (especially after no response to reasonable attempts to contact) can be disposed of or sold by the remaining tenant to avoid liability. - **Ethical responsibility:** You didn't "steal" or " take advantage"— you gave him ample opportunity to claim his belongings. His anger is purely about losing $600, not about any legitimate ethical or legal violation. **Final verdict:** You did the right thing. If he genuinely cared about the games, he would have responded to your messages. His " I'm an asshole" is just him being upset about the money, not a valid judgment of your actions. **You're not the asshole.** 💡 *(P.S. Next time, document all communication and consider involving the landlord formally if items remain— but in this case, you handled it perfectly.)*
